key_insight: Small-radius, high-electronegativity A-site dopants like Ca in BaCeO3 can simultaneously improve proton transport and chemical stability by weakening A–O bonding, increasing vacancy/proton uptake, and reducing gas adsorption.
engineering_relevance: A-site doping provides a practical design lever for proton-conducting Ba-based electrolytes, potentially enabling more durable solid oxide fuel cell materials with lower grain-boundary resistance.
method: Mechanistic analysis linking A-site electronegativity and ionic radius to vacancy formation, proton uptake, and gas adsorption.
Assessment of lattice contraction, impurity-phase suppression, and surface segregation effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computational evidence that Ca doping weakens A–O interactions, lowers adsorption strength for CO2/SO2, and can improve proton diffusion when proton transfer is rate-limiting.
watch_item: The benefits may depend on doping level, operating conditions, and whether Ca segregation or lattice contraction introduces trade-offs in real microstructures.
paper_title: Role of small-radius and high-electronegativity A-Site dopants in enhancing proton transport and stability of perovskite electrolytes
